definitions.explanation: A large, very sweet citrus variety identified by a distinctive bump (デコ) at the top. A hybrid of ponkan and a Kiyomi orange, mostly grown in Kumamoto and Ehime.

examples.japanese: デコポンは{頭|あたま}にこぶがある。
examples.english: Dekopons have a bump on top.

examples.japanese: デコポンはみかんより{大|おお}きくて{甘|あま}い。
examples.english: Dekopons are bigger and sweeter than regular mandarins.

examples.japanese: {熊本|くまもと}は{全国|ぜんこく}{一|いち}のデコポンの{産地|さんち}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: Kumamoto is known as the top dekopon-producing region in Japan.

notes:
The name combines デコ (bump) + ポン (from ポンカン, one of the parent varieties). Officially the variety is {不知火|しらぬい}; デコポン is a registered brand name for the highest-grade fruit. In daily speech, almost everyone uses デコポン regardless of grade.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- デコポンの{皮|かわ}を{剥|む}く: to peel a dekopon
- {熊本|くまもと}{産|さん}デコポン: Kumamoto-grown dekopon

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不知火|しらぬい}: shiranui — the official variety name; same fruit, non-brand
- {温州|うんしゅう}みかん: satsuma mandarin — much smaller, milder, no top bump
